A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RFDS, iRFDS and RFDS-Rev. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding equations, experiments, tables and figures can be matched despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation, image-editing, T3Bench, user-preference and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds SD3 and diffusion-model evaluations, including generation, editing and sensitivity results.

M1.justification: v3 extends the rectified-flow-specific objectives to schedule-dependent interpolation objectives and introduces a score-to-velocity adaptation for applying iRFDS and RFDS-Rev to diffusion models (Section 3.4). The alternating reversal/distillation procedure remains. The revised InstaFlow residual and weight signs preserve its original update rather than establishing a separate algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate text-guided 2D generation, T3Bench's three text-to-3D categories, and editing of internet images with three edits per image. Added backbones and qualitative examples do not establish a new dataset, domain or task.

E2.justification: The editing comparisons remove Rectified Flow Time Inversion from Table 2 and Figures 5 and 11, while adding SD3 and diffusion iRFDS variants. Figure 3 adds diffusion RFDS-Rev. DDS, Null Inversion, SDS, VSD and the RFDS-VSD ablation comparator remain in their corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 adds SD3 evaluations and diffusion implementations of the proposed methods. T3Bench reporting changes from quality, alignment and combined averages to quality alone. The editing user study changes from four choices to five, as shown in the screenshots and Table 2, although Appendix J retains four-method wording. Both versions report 15 editing images and the same original 3D optimization budget.

E4.justification: The existing noise-step, CFG and convergence analyses gain SD3 conditions (Figures 6, 8 and 10). The noise-step sweep drops n=4 while retaining n=0,1,2. These extend existing sensitivity questions; the Jacobian and RFDS-VSD ablations were already present in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the results. Revised user-preference percentages remain point estimates without uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains the original per-category quality scores but removes alignment results; RFDS-Rev's 49.3 combined average becomes a 48.9 quality-only average. SD3 RFDS-Rev adds quality scores of 59.8, 54.5 and 55.2. Table 2 adds SD3/diffusion CLIP scores of 0.297/0.296, and InstaFlow preference changes from 55.5% to 45.3% under different choices, not a comparable performance decline. Table 3 changes iRFDS's reported forward-pass count from two to one.

T1.justification: Sections 2–3 introduce general interpolation schedules, conditional-expectation velocity equations and generalized gradient derivations. Assumption 1 is narrowed to Reflow-finetuned models. New Appendix A derives score-based expressions and claims RFDS/SDS equivalence, although Equation 11 appears to omit the time derivative on the coefficient multiplying x_t.

C1.justification: v3 broadens the introduction's claims from rectified-flow priors to applicability across flow-matching and score-matching models. It newly claims RFDS/SDS equivalence and diffusion extensions of iRFDS and RFDS-Rev. The original claims of strong text-to-3D generation and competitive editing remain.

C2.justification: v3 makes Reflow central to its mechanism explanation and interprets the differing benefits on InstaFlow, SD3 and diffusion models. It acknowledges SD3's stronger backbone and training data, adds the unresolved CFG-mismatch limitation, and discusses memory obstacles to RFDS-VSD on SD3. The existing multi-face limitation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies RFDS-Rev noise-update step sizes: 1 for InstaFlow and 1−σ_t for SD3. It adds SD3's approximately one-hour runtime and model-specific weighting conventions. Existing hardware, optimization budgets, inversion regularization and code access remain; the newly stated InstaFlow step size does not establish a changed setting.

R1.justification: v3 substantially repositions the method within the general Stochastic Interpolants and diffusion PF-ODE frameworks, adding Albergo et al. (2023) and Song et al.'s SDE work as foundations. It also adds SiT and evaluation-related references. The original diffusion-prior review remains, but the relationship to SDS becomes an explicit equivalence claim.

P1.justification: The preliminaries and method rationale are substantially rewritten around generalized interpolants. v3 adds a diffusion-application subsection, revises the experimental narrative, expands Section 5 into an observations summary, and reorganizes the appendices from A.1–A.9 into A–J.

P2.justification: Comparison grids are extensively rearranged and expanded, Tables 1–2 gain backbone-specific columns, and Table 1 loses its metric subrows. CFG and convergence figures gain SD3 rows. Two SD3 galleries are added, while v1 Figures 12–13 are retained as v3 Figures 14–15. Algorithm placement and the document template also change.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens applicability evidence beyond v1's InstaFlow evaluations and more carefully scopes the Reflow rationale, limitations and implementation guidance. These gains are partly offset by removing alignment and direct time-inversion evidence, retaining an inconsistent user-study description, and introducing an apparent derivative omission in Equation 11. The resulting quality improvement is positive but qualified.
